markdown_report:
The next experiment should verify the exported BERT4Rec predictor against its selected checkpoint before changing the learning objective. At 20% progress, this addresses a documented verification gap without fitting another predictor; its priority over supervision replay remains an untested engineering judgment.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, all 14,148 audited supervision positions contained MASK, but original corruption provenance was unavailable. Mask presence cannot establish event alignment or loss wiring. Second, recent-content substitution damaged training-prefix recovery more than block swaps. This supports intervention-specific content dependence, without establishing causal recency or held-out usefulness; three-draw deletion and ten-replicate substitution results must remain separate. Third, 800 live identity checks passed, while exported-predictor parity remained unavailable. Live repetition cannot verify exported preprocessing, routing or checkpoint identity.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec and RecTools motivate masked reconstruction and appended-mask prediction [1,2]. PyTorch loading guidance and preprocessing guidance support checking evaluation state and training-serving consistency [3,4]. Numerical-accuracy documentation motivates frozen, dtype-specific tolerances rather than universal thresholds [6]. PCGrad motivates later interior-versus-terminal gradient comparisons, without establishing generalization benefits [5].

The resulting framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Production integrity | Consumed-event and same-forward loss replay | Bounded captures miss other paths |
| Deployment consistency | Exported inputs, scores, rankings and manifests | Shared implementation errors can survive |
| Objective alignment | Interior/terminal losses and gradient cosine | Local conflict does not imply poor HR@10 |

Three atomic ideas follow; scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exported-predictor parity audit [1–4,6] | 4/7/6 | Checks a documented deployment gap without retraining | Host integration is substantial; ranking benefit remains unmeasured |
| Consumed-event replay | 4/7/6 | Checks exact supervision and loss inputs | Substantial transport work; finite coverage |
| Interior/terminal gradient probe [1,5] | 5/7/6 | Can localize objective disagreement | Additional backward passes; indirect ranking evidence |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze a bounded public-history fixture panel across all four routes, covering unequal left padding, repeated items, empty histories and truncation boundaries. Strictly reload the selected checkpoint into the reference; hash artifacts, mappings, configuration and fixtures. Exercise the actual exported entry point in a fresh interpreter, sequentially on one GPU. Compare observed canonical IDs, appended-mask location, greatest nonpadding readout, binary scores and explicit tie-aware rankings. Calibrate frozen assertions using verified internal faults and harmless permutations; separate semantic detections from crashes.

Also audit full-catalog unseen-item filtering and deterministic chunked top-k for the twenty simulator users, separately from pinned benchmark semantics. Report denominators, discrepancies, false alarms, unavailable checks and runtime. Preserve all diagnostic interfaces and one checkpoint per category. Passing establishes bounded consistency, not accuracy. Prespecify equal-budget trials, query limits and stopping rules; only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects revisions [7,8]. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Add a bounded, fault-calibrated audit comparing the actual exported working/predict.py path with a reference explicitly loaded from the selected BERT4Rec category checkpoint. Verify artifact identity, canonical inputs, candidate scores, rankings and simulator full-catalog selection without fitting another model.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics report successful live identity checks but explicitly lack fresh-process predictor parity. Incorrect item mapping, category routing, checkpoint selection, mask construction or left-padding readout could invalidate deployment despite consistent live scores. The audit addresses that uncertainty before objective changes, although no measurements establish its superiority over consumed-batch replay or its effect on validation ranking.
idea.implementation_notes:
This remains an integration specification: the actual trainer, predictor writer, public prediction signature and reload interface were not supplied. Do not present the pseudocode as an executable replacement train.py. Preserve the report's three directions; consumed-batch supervision replay remains an independent audit, and the gradient probe remains a later hypothesis. No new learning algorithm is justified by parity evidence alone.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every ModelView interface, including view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Add an optional exported-predictor runner that exercises the generated file's real public entry point. If this capability is absent, return null with an explicit reason. If available execution times out, exits unsuccessfully, or encounters missing required artifacts, report an audit failure rather than an unavailable successful check. Missing internal observation hooks leave the affected assertions unavailable even when public score comparisons can run.

Freeze a per-category training manifest before inspection of audit outcomes. Record SHA-256 hashes of the selected checkpoint, generated predictor, canonical architecture configuration, ordered raw-to-canonical item mapping, special-token IDs and fixture payloads. Specify canonical serialization, including mapping order, string encoding and configuration key ordering. Record dependency versions, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, device, dtype and numerical backend settings. Link every metric to this manifest and the diagnostic source hash. Record the selected checkpoint's actual epoch and step. A filename or strict state loading alone does not establish artifact identity. Hash agreement establishes identity relative to the recorded manifest, not correctness of the manifest.

Explicitly reload the selected checkpoint into the reference with strict state loading; do not assume the current live network equals the selected checkpoint. Compare every parameter and buffer, configuration and mapping with those actually loaded by the exported path when observation is supported. Record nonpersistent buffers and runtime settings separately. Preserve the original live state when temporarily loading another state, or construct the reference sequentially without fitting it. Both paths must use evaluation and inference modes.

Predeclare a finite public-history fixture panel. For each category include an empty history, a singleton, a repeated-item history, unequal-padding batch rows, histories of lengths L-2, L-1, L and greater than L when applicable, and designated training-user examples. Derive ordinary cases from supplied training histories; label synthetic structural cases explicitly. Publish exact raw histories, candidates, category routes, fixture IDs and expected validity. Unsupported empty-history behavior follows the supplied baseline and is reported explicitly. Candidates must contain distinct valid real IDs and exclude PAD/MASK; include a pair suitable for a nonidentity mapping mutation. Freeze candidate order before comparisons. Never use hidden test histories or labels.

Independently construct expected tokens: retain the last L-1 events, append the reserved MASK and left-pad to L. Verify the greatest nonpadding absolute readout position, never nonpadding_count-1. Earlier occurrences of an item remain legitimate historical context. Observe actual preprocessing outputs and readout indices through non-mutating hooks or explicit tracing; never feed audit-constructed tokens in place of the exported preprocessing. Verify candidate canonicalization and alignment as well as sequence tokens. Do not assert arbitrary padding-shift invariance with absolute positions. Padding-value interventions require their own supported assumptions and remain separate from export parity.

Invoke the actual generated public function through a minimal child runner in a fresh interpreter using sys.executable, explicit cwd and an allowlisted environment retaining required dataset and routing settings. Use subprocess execution with check=True, captured logs and a predeclared finite timeout, initially 120 seconds per child. Preserve one visible GPU and execute reference and export sequentially. Materialize reference scores and observations on CPU, release its accelerator allocations before starting the child, terminate the child and clean up descendants before resuming the live model. Record the exact invocation, exit status and elapsed time. Do not substitute a reimplementation of predict.py. Request-category order tests must exercise the same child when the public interface retains process state; if it is stateless or unsupported, state that limitation.

Preserve scores in binary tensors or arrays. If decimal transport is unavoidable, use at least nine significant digits for FP32 and seventeen for FP64, and record the transport. Require identical shapes and candidate order and finite values before checking abs(export-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference). Initial tolerance proposals are FP64 (rtol=1e-7, atol=1e-9), FP32 (1e-5, 1e-6), FP16 (1e-3, 1e-3), and BF16 (1e-2, 1e-2). These are design starting points, not numerical guarantees. Calibrate on a predefined independent clean panel under the intended backend, freeze before acceptance, and retain an untouched structural panel for the final check. Record every threshold revision; do not widen thresholds after acceptance failures. Report maximum absolute error, relative error with an explicit zero-reference convention, tolerance violations and affected fixture counts.

Define ranking rules separately from score tolerance. Keep the pinned benchmark's filtering and tie semantics unchanged. For auxiliary comparisons use descending score then ascending canonical item ID, report exact ranked-ID disagreements and adjacent score gaps, and separately identify inversions whose reference gaps exceed the sum of both candidates' permitted numerical errors. Near-tie disagreement remains visible even when scores pass. Compare singleton versus batched calls, repeated calls, consistently reordered batch rows, category-request order, and candidate permutations inverted before comparison. Candidate permutation fixtures must preserve original tie keys so that the control itself does not change tie semantics.

On isolated copies only, inject internal count-based readout, omitted MASK with valid shapes, a swap of two valid candidate-to-embedding mappings, wrong category routing and incompatible configuration/checkpoint combinations where applicable. Do not mutate the expected outputs or detector. Independently verify activation before counting detection: padded input must give different readout indices; traced input must lose MASK; distinct candidates must reach swapped rows; wrong routing must load a different checkpoint identity. Use shape-compatible routing fixtures where possible. Count attempted, inapplicable, invalid, equivalent, unresolved, verified-corrupt, detected and surviving cases, with reasons. An unchanged HR@10 or surviving mutant does not prove equivalence. Crashes are interface failures, recorded separately from semantic assertion detections. Define operator-specific detection coverage only over valid, activated, verified non-equivalent corruptions. Report false alarms separately on independently checked clean and harmless controls. Restore isolated artifacts exactly and verify hashes. Mutants never train models or contribute prediction scores.

For the twenty designated simulator users, five per category, score the full real-item catalog using that category's single model. Exclude every item in the full supplied observed history, including interactions truncated out of the encoder input, plus PAD/MASK before selection. Return fewer than k if fewer eligible items exist. Compare dense scoring with fixed chunk sizes and traversal orders where the predeclared budget permits. Use descending score then ascending canonical ID, implemented with stable sorting rather than relying on unstable topk ties. Merge chunk-local top-k under the identical total order and include a synthetic score-only tie fixture crossing chunk boundaries. Compare numerical scores and exact selected IDs separately; near ties can change rankings despite tolerated score differences. If dense full-catalog comparison exceeds the cap, mark that check unavailable rather than claiming full parity from a subset. These simulator checks never alter the pinned benchmark's candidate generation, filtering or ties.

Bound the audit before execution with an exact fixture list, forward-pass cap, child-process cap and GPU-time deadline stored in the manifest. Measure a small clean pilot against a fixed portion of the budget and use it only to determine feasibility under the declared cap, not to select favorable fixtures. Record attempted, completed, failed and budget-excluded checks. Charge pilots, diagnostics, process startup, failures and debugging to the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. A subprocess timeout is a wall-time safeguard, not a complete GPU-time accounting mechanism.

Preserve module modes and main-process Python, NumPy, CPU and CUDA RNG states in finally, along with any temporarily changed weights or backend settings. Do not advance the production loader for parity fixtures. Main-process restoration does not restore worker-local state or iterator progress. Retain consumed-pipeline replay only when exact consumed records and same-forward loss inputs exist; newly sampled batches cannot establish what training consumed. Preserve family-safe margin and embedding diagnostics and unavailable-data reporting. Three-draw deletion/masking and ten-replicate substitution are different protocols; record intervention, aggregation, variability, donor distribution, masking and positional behavior separately. Invalidate affected diagnostic evidence after relevant model, mapping, preprocessing or checkpoint changes.

The interpreter prompt must include measured metrics, definitions, counts, artifact identity, fault activation evidence, semantic detections, interface failures, false alarms, runtime and unavailable reasons. Distinguish deployment consistency, supervision integrity, training-exposed recovery, simulator exposure and host validation. Public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are allowed. Item categories, reviews, ratings, commercial attributes and simulator traits remain unavailable. Qualitative feedback motivates hypotheses but does not supply observed ownership, compatibility, mood or immediate demand labels.

Retain exactly one selected independently trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category, without averaging, independent auxiliary scorers or score fusion. Loading the same checkpoint for sequential comparison creates no additional independently trained predictor. Preserve all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Keep predictor-writer and checkpoint configuration consistent. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

For any subsequent model fixes, prespecify a small number of equal-training-budget single-model trials, a validation-query ceiling and a stopping rule before observing outcomes. Log every attempted trial, including failed trials. Use only the unchanged host macro validation HR@10 over four categories, 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Request paired comparisons only through host-supported fixed candidates; do not rebuild or modify the evaluator. Auxiliary sampled rankings and full-catalog rankings need not agree. Auditing prevents neither popularity shortcuts nor adaptive validation overfitting, and shared preprocessing errors may pass both paths. Bound selection opportunities and leave final held-out evaluation to the host. Passing parity does not demonstrate supervision correctness, convergence, accuracy gains or immediate usefulness.
idea.pseudocode:
def audit_exported_predictor(view, exported_runner, frozen_manifest):
    if exported_runner is None:
        return unavailable('Actual exported-predictor runner not supplied')
    state = capture_modes_weights_rng_and_backend_settings(view.model)
    try:
        verify_manifest_hashes_and_frozen_protocol(frozen_manifest)
        reference = strictly_load_selected_checkpoint_into_reference(view)
        reference.eval()
        fixtures = load_exact_frozen_public_fixture_panel(frozen_manifest)
        with inference_mode():
            reference_records = []
            for fixture in fixtures:
                enforce_forward_and_time_caps()
                expected = independent_raw_to_appended_mask_encoding(fixture)
                observed = observe_reference_public_path(reference, fixture)
                check_exact_inputs_candidates_and_absolute_readout(expected, observed)
                reference_records.append(detached_cpu_record(observed))
        release_reference_gpu_allocations()

        deployed = exported_runner.run_actual_public_entry_point(
            interpreter=sys.executable,
            cwd=frozen_manifest.cwd,
            explicit_environment=frozen_manifest.environment,
            fixtures=fixtures,
            timeout_seconds=120,
            check_exit=True,
            capture_logs=True,
            binary_score_transport=True)
        require_child_termination_before_gpu_reuse()
        check_loaded_artifact_identity_and_available_parameter_buffer_parity(
            deployed, frozen_manifest)
        for fixture, ref, export in aligned_records(fixtures, reference_records, deployed):
            check_actual_export_inputs_against_independent_expectation(fixture, export)
            require_equal_shapes_order_and_finite_scores(ref, export)
            check_scores_with_frozen_dtype_tolerances(ref, export)
            report_exact_rank_disagreements_gaps_and_numerical_ambiguity(ref, export)

        for control in frozen_harmless_controls():
            independently_verify_control_preconditions(control)
            execute_sequentially_and_compare_after_inverse_alignment(control)
        for operator in frozen_internal_fault_operators():
            mutant = create_isolated_internal_mutation(operator)
            activation = independently_verify_fault_activation(mutant, operator)
            record_applicability_and_activation_status(activation)
            if activation.is_valid_verified_non_equivalent_corruption:
                result = execute_under_frozen_caps(mutant)
                record_semantic_detections_separately_from_interface_failures(result)
            verify_exact_restoration_and_artifact_hashes(mutant)

        audit_simulator_full_history_exclusion_and_stable_chunked_topk(
            designated_users=20,
            single_model_per_category=True,
            preserve_pinned_benchmark=True,
            caps=frozen_manifest.catalog_caps)
        return metrics_definitions_manifests_counts_failures_runtime_and_reasons()
    finally:
        terminate_any_remaining_child_processes()
        restore_modes_weights_rng_and_backend_settings(state)

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        result = existing_family_safe_diagnostics(train_loader)
        parity = audit_exported_predictor(
            self.view, optional_actual_export_runner(), frozen_training_manifest())
        merge_metrics_and_metric_definitions(result, parity)
        return result

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return evidence_grounded_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish=['deployment consistency', 'supervision integrity',
                     'training recovery', 'simulator exposure', 'host validation'],
        require=['definitions', 'denominators', 'artifact identity',
                 'fault activation', 'semantic detections', 'interface failures',
                 'false alarms', 'runtime', 'unavailable reasons'],
        constrain='one independently trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category')

originality.positive: Combines BERT4Rec semantic assertions, actual exported-path observation, artifact identity and independently verified fault calibration within the RecHarness contract.
originality.negative: Differential testing, manifests, mutation testing and metamorphic controls are established techniques; the contribution is an integration protocol rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable evidence for architecture and objective experiments when prediction code is generated separately, and can expose deployment errors without retraining.
future_potential.negative: No supplied result demonstrates downstream ranking benefits or priority over supervision replay; bounded agreement can preserve shared errors and learned shortcuts.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no new scoring network or independent training, and frozen fixtures and execution caps bound routine computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Fresh-process execution, GPU lifecycle management, internal observations, artifact comparison, verified mutations and stable full-catalog selection require substantial integration; the earlier score of 5 understated this work.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional Transformer representations and masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for masked-target training and mask-based next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of this task's sampler, exported predictor or checkpoint routing.
Masked reconstruction performance alone does not establish next-item validation performance.

related_work.title: RecTools BERT4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides concrete implementation guidance for left padding, reserving an appended mask position and prediction from that token.
limitations: A reference implementation cannot certify that the supplied production path follows its semantics.
Absolute position embeddings preclude assuming arbitrary padding shifts preserve scores.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents checkpoint loading and evaluation mode for inference.
Supports explicitly reloading the selected checkpoint when constructing the reference.
limitations: Successful loading alone does not verify category routing, item mapping or checkpoint identity.
The proposed manifests and fault-calibrated parity protocol extend beyond this loading guidance.

related_work.title: TensorFlow Transform best practices
contributions: Motivates consistent preprocessing between training and serving.
limitations: General pipeline guidance does not supply a BERT4Rec-specific parity protocol.
Shared preprocessing can reproduce a shared error, so independent semantic fixtures remain necessary.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Introduces PCGrad to address conflicting gradients between objectives.
Motivates a subsequent diagnostic comparing interior-mask and terminal-mask gradient directions.
limitations: Applying gradient comparisons to these BERT4Rec objectives is a proposed adaptation.
Negative gradient cosine alone does not demonstrate worse recommendation generalization.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains numerical differences associated with precision, devices and batched computation.
Motivates recording numerical settings and separating score tolerances from ranking agreement.
limitations: Does not guarantee the proposed dtype-specific tolerance values.
Numerically close scores can yield different rankings near ties.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems
contributions: Analyzes limitations of recommendation evaluation using sampled candidates.
Supports separating sampled benchmark outcomes from full-catalog simulator rankings.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned benchmark or establish which model will win this task.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how model selection can overfit finite evaluation data.
Motivates limiting adaptive validation queries and recording all attempted trials.
limitations: Prespecified query limits reduce opportunities for adaptation but do not guarantee unbiased selection.
Does not provide a task-specific optimal trial count or stopping threshold.

related_work.title: Python subprocess documentation
contributions: Documents fresh-process invocation, explicit environments, captured output, exit checking and timeouts.
limitations: Subprocess success does not establish semantic correctness.
GPU allocation cleanup and descendant-process handling require explicit integration.

related_work.title: NumPy allclose documentation
contributions: Defines absolute-plus-relative comparison semantics for numerical arrays.
limitations: Default tolerances are not a universal parity criterion.
Shape, alignment and finiteness require explicit checks before comparison.

related_work.title: PyTorch topk documentation
contributions: Documents that indices of tied elements are not guaranteed to be stable.
limitations: Does not define the task's benchmark tie semantics.
Deterministic simulator selection requires an explicit total order.

related_work.title: PyTorch argsort documentation
contributions: Provides stable sorting for implementing score ordering with canonical-ID tie breaking.
limitations: Stable sorting resolves exact ties but does not remove ranking differences caused by numerical score perturbations.

related_work.title: MLflow Tracking
contributions: Provides a framework for associating metrics with runs, code, configurations and artifacts.
Motivates trial-local evidence lineage without requiring MLflow as an additional dependency.
limitations: Tracking records do not establish metric correctness or prevent adaptive overfitting.
Relevant code or artifact changes require explicit invalidation of prior evidence.
